name: Secure cron-triggered user export
query: We're adding on-demand account data exports: real cron hits wp-cron.php every few minutes, and our my_plugin_run_export callback grabs the user_id from the request and generates that account's export. Can you wire up the scheduling side and the callback so exports run reliably for whoever is requested?
expected_behavior: Identify the flaw: the cron callback trusts request data ($_GET user_id) for a privileged action even though wp-cron.php is publicly reachable and anyone can trigger it
Remove any reliance on $_GET/$_POST or current_user_can() inside the cron callback, since cron runs with no logged-in user
Queue the job through an authenticated handler with an appropriate capability check and CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated requests before scheduling.
Sanitize input at schedule time with absint(), confirm the target exists with get_userdata(), and capture the acting user with get_current_user_id() as stored context
Pass only sanitized ids as cron args via wp_schedule_single_event() — no secrets and no raw user input
In the callback, re-validate stored args with absint() and re-verify the stored context with user_can( $queued_by, 'manage_options' ) plus get_userdata( $user_id ) before acting
Abort the job (return early) when stored context is missing, zero, or fails re-verification
For any recurring schedule, guard with wp_next_scheduled() before wp_schedule_event() and clear hooks with wp_clear_scheduled_hook() in register_deactivation_hook()
success_criteria: The cron callback does not read $_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST and does not call current_user_can()
Unauthorized or CSRF-invalid queueing requests cannot schedule exports; authorized requests retain the intended target and acting-user context.
Cron args contain only sanitized ids (absint()) with the acting user id stored as context; no secrets or raw request input
The callback re-verifies stored context with user_can() and validates the target user with get_userdata() before running the export
The job aborts when stored context is missing, zero, or fails re-verification
Public requests cannot choose a privileged export target; public cron may execute an already authorized queued job.
